definition: Edward Albert Feigenbaum (born January 20, 1936) is an American computer scientist working in the field of artificial intelligence, and with Raj Reddy he won the 1994 ACM Turing Award.
details: Created DENDRAL and MYCIN, demonstrating how domain-specific knowledge bases could solve complex scientific and medical problems. He is often called the "father of expert systems".

explainer.lead: Edward Feigenbaum is an American computer scientist. His work spans computer science, informatics, artificial intelligence and expert system.

contributions.name: Feigenbaum took a course "Mathematical Models in the Social Sciences" taught by Simon, where Simon announced the Logic Theorist with "Over the Christmas holidays, Al Newell and I invented a thinking machine." Simon gave Feigenbaum a manual of IBM 701, which he read in one night.
He also co-founded companies IntelliCorp and Teknowledge.

In January 2026, the Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI) honored Feigenbaum at its 40th annual conference in Singapore in celebration of his 90th birthday, recognizing his foundational contributions to the field of expert systems.
